# Independent audit: the globally critical nongluing trapezoids

Audited sources:

- `candidate c0a17a15efbe8efa`
- `supporting computation verify_truncated_triangle_globalcritical_cap_gluing.py`

Result: PASS. The verifier was independently rerun to completion and
reported all 672 rational Bernstein polynomial certificates nonnegative.
The audit below verifies why those certificates cover all ambient
halfspaces and why the example has the claimed exact geometry. It is
an auxiliary gluing counterexample, not a counterexample to OC.

## Actual body and the three special caps

The listed inequalities define a bounded full-dimensional convex body:
the integer coordinate is in [-1,1], and the positive first quadrant
is truncated between the two sloping planes h<=x+y<=1+epsilon z.
The three integer fibers are exactly K_(1-epsilon), K_1, K_(1+epsilon).
The four cyclic vertices (h,0),(r,0),(0,r),(0,h) give area
(r^2-h^2)/2 by the determinant formula. Direct rational calculations
independently confirm every quoted area, total M, noheavy margin,
Q/M=182000000/405433227, and delta/|K|>4/9. They also confirm
Q/M>12/29, as required by the independent strict-margin theorem.

The midpoint of each pair of corresponding endpoint vertices is a
middle vertex, proving K subset (A+B)/2; the four common-normal
inequalities give the reverse inclusion. The equal positive inner
edge lengths force any positive homothety ratio to be one, whereas
the outer edges have different lengths. Thus the endpoints really
are not positive homothets.

For H_1, every captured piece is the common frustum because
0<h<2t<1-epsilon. For H_2, substituting (x,y)->(x-epsilon z,y)
removes z from both the cut equation and the upper sum inequality.
Its middle triangle has the three displayed vertices. The minimum
x+y over that triangle is 4t-1; after translation it is at least
4t-1-epsilon>h. Its minimum x is positive because both
4t-1-epsilon>h>0 and 1-2t-epsilon>0. Thus the discarded quadrant and
inner-sum inequalities are indeed nonbinding. H_3 follows by coordinate
exchange. This proves the actual cap-set identities and properness,
not merely equal numerical areas. Their areas are delta, so each
mixed mass is exactly Q=3delta.

The positive balance concerns only the continuous normals:
(t,3t-1)+(3t-1,t)=(4t-1)(1,1). Accordingly the three middle traces
cover the continuous plane. Their full ambient normals have a residual
integer-coordinate sum -2epsilon t and are not positively balanced.
No full mixed-set cover by these three particular caps is used.

## Exhaustiveness of the orientation reduction

Moving any containing halfspace parallel to place Y on its boundary
reduces its captured set. A pure integer normal then gives one full
endpoint together with the full middle fiber, including the entire
boundary fiber. Both resulting masses exceed Q. Thus boundary mass
for vertical halfspaces is accounted for explicitly.

For any nonzero continuous normal, coordinate exchange makes its
first component have largest absolute value. Reversing the halfspace
if needed and dividing by that positive component gives (1,k),
-1<=k<=1, with an unrestricted integer coefficient alpha. Reversal
is legitimate because the proof establishes both bounds
Q<=P<=M-Q: nonvertical boundaries have zero area in every fiber,
so opposite caps sum to M. This handles oblique halfspaces of every
orientation and both signs.

The area of the frustum cut is exactly the outer-triangle tail minus
the inner-triangle tail. The two three-branch proper formulas for
positive and negative k follow from the ordered vertex values
(0,kr,r) and (kr,0,r), respectively; they agree with their full and
zero branches at the breakpoints. Consequently formula (7) in the
source is the actual mixed cap area throughout every strip.

For |alpha|>=2, both endpoint cuts have saturated, one full and
one empty. This follows directly from 0<=t(1+k)<=2t<1 and
all triangle vertex values in [-1-epsilon,1+epsilon]. Thus the
alpha-dependent sum is constant beyond the two end strips. No
unbounded family of omitted tilt directions remains.

## Exact finite certificate and every partition boundary

The endpoint branch transitions are precisely the affine alpha
functions at values 0,kr,r for the two endpoint outer triangles and
the common inner triangle. Their pairwise intersections partition
the k-axis wherever their ordering could change. The separate roots
for the middle fiber are included because its level does not depend
on alpha. The additional lines and the equality-direction split
only refine this exhaustive partition.

In each open k interval, distinct affine boundary lines have a fixed
strict ordering. The 14 consecutive strips between the 15 lines
cover the entire alpha interval [-2,2]. Evaluating branches at the
rational interior midpoint is therefore valid throughout the open
strip, rather than a numerical sampling assertion. The rerun generated
17 positive-k intervals and 7 negative-k intervals, hence exactly
24*14*2=672 inequality polynomials.

The multiplier 2 sign(k) k(1-k) is strictly positive in every open
strip under consideration. It clears all variable denominators of
the exact triangle formulas. The affine-in-alpha strip map followed
by the affine k map gives a rational polynomial on the entire unit
square. Its separate-degree tensor Bernstein expansion has exactly
the coefficients given by formula (16); the formula follows by
expanding each monomial in the binomial basis. Every basis term is
nonnegative on the square and their sum is one. Thus nonnegative
coefficients are a valid exact sufficient certificate, including on
all strip edges. The verifier uses symbolic rational arithmetic and
reconstructs all numerators and coefficients; it does not read the
stored positive minima as assumptions. No mesh or floating-point
test is used.

At k=0 or k=1 the clearing multiplier can vanish. The desired
original cap-area inequalities still follow by continuity from
neighboring orientations, because in every fixed full-dimensional
fiber a nonzero continuous boundary normal gives a line of area
zero. The same dominated-convergence argument covers k=-1 and all
other strip boundaries. Closed nonvertical halfspaces therefore
require no separate missing boundary correction.

## Exact depth and scope

The certificate proves that every ambient halfspace through Y captures
at least Q, and each of the three displayed caps attains Q. Hence
Y is a single deterministic mixed-integer point of depth Q/M.
Every middle-fiber point belongs to one displayed cap, giving its
depth upper bound Q. The endpoint fibers are separately isolated by
the closed vertical caps z<=-1 and z>=1, of mass less than Q.
Thus the exact global maximal raw depth is Q.

All proper endpoint cuts, exact captured-side BM equalities, genuine
global criticality, and source-fiber trace cover hypotheses of the
three-fiber strict-margin theorem hold. The example therefore rules
out general global homothety from those hypotheses while respecting
that theorem. It does not address a stronger premise requiring the
same three ambient halfspaces to cover the entire mixed set, nor a
premise requiring the same continuous offset in every fiber.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
